caption: The drawing depicts a stone wall with an arched doorway at the center. The walls are rendered in shades of gray and beige, showing the texture of the stone blocks. The arched doorway features a pair of closed, double wooden doors colored in faded blue-gray tones, flanked by yellowish-brown stone columns. Above the arch, there are three skull and crossbones symbols depicted in black and gray, with one directly above the center and two symmetrically placed to the left and right. There is a rectangular barred window above the main arch. The ground in front of the door is covered by a reddish-brown tiled surface, with each tile outlined in white. To the right of the door, there is a stone structure, which may be a low wall or bench, shown in shades of gray. On the ground near this structure, there are two objects resembling shoes, colored in brown and dark tones. The drawing is set against a plain background, with no additional objects or scenery.
title: Doorway and Doors
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
